clean_story:
Scatter seeds. Grow new plants.

The term seed dispersal describes how seeds travel away from their parent plant to sprout elsewhere. A coconut falls into the ocean, floats on saltwater like a tiny boat, and drifts to a new island. A burdock hook clings to animal fur like a natural Velcro, hitching a ride to fresh soil. Some seeds explode, flinging themselves meters away with a built-in spring. Others rely on wind, spinning like helicopter blades to slow their fall. Without this movement, seedlings would crowd each other, competing for sunlight and water. Records show the Brazil nut tree depends on agoutis to bury its seeds, forgetting some, which then grow into new trees. Three related subjects are fruit adaptations, animal migration and forest regeneration.
